Claim: ADS = max(c_i)/sum(c_i), a per-product historical determinism metric, is a measurement contribution.
PriorArtOverlap: Identical closed-form to cluster purity (Manning et al. 2008; Amigo et al. 2009; Zhao & Karypis 2003) and to the majority-vote-agreement baseline in the Dawid & Skene (1979) truth-inference lineage (confirmed by Uma et al. 2021; Davani et al. 2021); near-identical to the informal 'percent agreement' construct in the Fleiss (1971) kappa lineage. Tier 1 direct prior art from two independent literatures.
DistinctiveElement: None at the level of the metric's construction. Only the unit of analysis (an item's historical booking multiset vs. a clustering output or annotator panel) differs -- a relabeling, not a mathematical difference.
TechnicalSignificance: None as a standalone claim. The metric contributes nothing beyond a renamed existing formula.
EmpiricallyTestable: N/A -- this is a mathematical-identity finding, not an empirical hypothesis. No experiment changes whether two formulas are identical.
CurrentEvidence: ads_metric_prior_art.md / ads_metric_prior_art.csv (rows G1-01..G1-09), closed in the 2026-08-11 gap-verification pass.
FalsificationTest: N/A (already falsified as a novelty claim; nothing further to test).
Risk: Citing ADS as a new metric is an easily-caught overclaim for any reviewer familiar with IR or crowdsourcing literature.

Claim: Historical per-item decision consistency (ADS), aggregated once and thresholded before deployment, is a valid design-time signal for choosing which CLASS of classification mechanism (rules / embedding-retrieval / LLM) to build -- not merely which algorithm or hyperparameters to pick within one fixed class.
PriorArtOverlap: General pattern (measure evidence once, choose architecture before serving) is well-precedented: Rice 1976 (ASP); Smith-Miles 2009; Barbudo et al. 2023 (AutoML 'workflow composition'); Ali & Smith 2006 / Khan et al. 2020 (meta-learning classifier selection); Idreos & Kraska 2019 / Kraska 2021 (self-designed data systems -- opposite temporal structure: continuous, not one-shot).
DistinctiveElement: Narrower combination not found in any of 79 reviewed sources: (a) the evidence type is restricted to label-consistency specifically, not workload frequency, cross-validated performance, or generic statistical meta-features, combined with (b) the decision output is a qualitative mechanism-CLASS choice, not an algorithm/hyperparameter choice within one class.
TechnicalSignificance: Potentially meaningful IF the ADS threshold value actually tracks where one mechanism class empirically outperforms another. Not yet shown -- the existing R1/R3 decisions are single threshold comparisons on one production dataset and one synthetic dataset, not a validated predictive relationship.
EmpiricallyTestable: Yes -- the one candidate with a clean, falsifiable empirical form. See experimental_design.md, Experiment 1.
CurrentEvidence: Two real data points only: production det_pct=91.2% -> RULES_FIRST; synthetic det_pct=87.56% -> EMBEDDING_PRIMARY (the 'R3 flip', r3_threshold_analysis.md). Neither run measured whether the selected mechanism actually outperformed the alternatives -- the rule has been exercised, never validated against measured mechanism performance.
MissingEvidence: A controlled sweep across ADS bands (approx. 0.60/0.70/0.80/0.90/0.95/0.99) with all three mechanism classes actually built and measured head-to-head, not just the selection rule exercised once per band. See Experiment 1.
FalsificationTest: If the empirically best-performing mechanism at a given ADS band systematically disagrees with the mechanism the current 0.90/0.70 threshold rule would select (e.g. embedding-primary beats rules-first at ADS=0.95, or rules-first beats LLM at ADS=0.60), the threshold values -- and possibly the qualitative claim -- are falsified.
Risk: This is a threshold heuristic exercised exactly twice, not a validated predictive relationship. C2b's narrower literature framing survives Phase B's challenge, but literature survival is not empirical validation.

Claim: Extraction confidence (OCR/structuring) and classification confidence (product->account) are computed independently by architecturally separate subsystems and never blended, to avoid conflating two different failure modes.
PriorArtOverlap: Liu, Gallego & Barbieri 2022 (B5-06) uses two related uncertainty terms to modulate one deferral decision -- the single strongest adversarial hit against this claim found in the sweep.
DistinctiveElement: B5-06's two terms come from the same model's internal uncertainty; ADS-Cascade's two signals come from two architecturally separate subsystems (a third-party OCR provider vs. an internal classification pipeline). A real but narrow distinction.
TechnicalSignificance: Modest. 'Don't blend two different-provenance confidence signals' is a reasonable engineering choice, but nothing in this repository shows blending would actually perform worse -- no ablation exists.
EmpiricallyTestable: Yes in principle (ablation: blended vs. unblended signal, measured on routing accuracy/coverage) -- not designed in this pass; would require building the counterfactual blended-signal router.
CurrentEvidence: ADR-007 states the design rationale; no ablation study exists comparing blended vs. unblended routing outcomes anywhere in this repository.
MissingEvidence: An ablation comparing routing accuracy/coverage with a single blended confidence score against the current two-signal design, on the same synthetic held-out set.
FalsificationTest: If a blended single-signal router achieves equal or better accuracy/coverage than the two-signal router on the same data, the distinction is cosmetic, not technically significant.
Risk: Narrow architectural distinction resting on one adversarial near-miss paper, with no ablation evidence that unblending actually improves outcomes. A reviewer could call this an implementation detail.

Claim: Every Tier-4 (human-corrected) resolution permanently promotes that product to Tier-1 for that company, without model retraining -- framed as the knowledge base's growth mechanism, not a failure state.
PriorArtOverlap: Human-correction-changes-future-behavior is decades old (active learning, interactive ML, machine teaching -- Mosqueira-Rey et al. 2022 survey). Beede et al. 2020 shows naive reject-to-human handoffs fail without such a mechanism (motivating evidence, not a competing method).
DistinctiveElement: The specific mechanism -- permanent, per-item, per-company promotion into an exact-match lookup tier, with no retraining step -- was not found described as such in any of 79 sources. Functionally close to a rule-engine exception-cache / override table, a common production pattern outside ML research.
TechnicalSignificance: Real for this system's engineering (the difference between staying broken on repeat errors and not), but the mechanism itself is a simple write-through cache keyed by human-verified label, and its value over that simpler framing has never been measured.
EmpiricallyTestable: Yes -- measure system behavior with the feedback loop enabled vs. disabled over a simulated transaction stream. See Experiment 3.
CurrentEvidence: Described in TECHNICAL_REPORT.md's tier table / ADR as a design decision. No before/after measurement exists anywhere in this repository -- no run has ever compared the loop on vs. off.
MissingEvidence: Before/after accuracy, automation-rate, and stabilization-time measurements with the loop enabled vs. disabled, plus a false-promotion robustness check. See Experiment 3.
FalsificationTest: If disabling the promotion loop produces no measurable degradation in automation rate or accuracy over a simulated multi-period transaction stream, the mechanism adds no demonstrated value beyond face-value plausibility. If a trivial 'always trust the last correction, no evidence weighting' baseline performs equivalently, the specific design adds nothing over a naive cache.
Risk: Highest reviewer risk of the six: even a successful experiment shows the mechanism WORKS, which is not the same as showing it is a research contribution rather than production-engineering competence.

Claim: The combined system -- Part 1 (determinism-driven design-time architecture selection) + Part 2 (runtime multi-tier cascade with feedback) -- is one coherent method whose value exceeds the sum of its individually-precedented parts.
PriorArtOverlap: Every individual component is well-precedented (see C1/C2/C3/C5 rows above, plus the LLM-reranking-constraint and cross-company-threshold components tracked separately in contribution_status.md). Monteiro et al. 2021 (B2-07) independently proposes a structurally similar two-phase shape, though its runtime phase is concept-drift retraining, a different mechanism.
DistinctiveElement: Zero Tier-1 sources combine all four elements (design-time label-consistency gate + dual-signal cascade + reranking-only LLM constraint + permanent human-promotion loop) into one system. This is combination novelty, not component novelty.
TechnicalSignificance: Combination novelty is intrinsically the weakest form of novelty claim -- reviewers routinely discount 'novel assembly of known parts' unless it demonstrates empirical value the parts lack separately, i.e. beats the best simple baseline on a real accuracy/cost frontier.
EmpiricallyTestable: Yes -- exactly what the cascade experiment (Experiment 2, baselines B1-B5) is designed to test.
CurrentEvidence: A held-out cascade eval exists (Tier-1 98.4% accuracy @ 42% coverage; full cascade 98.1% @ 42.8% coverage) but has never been compared against any of the four simpler baselines (rules-only, retrieval-only, LLM-only, fixed-order cascade) on the same data.
MissingEvidence: Head-to-head B1-B5 comparison on accuracy, coverage, automation rate, human-review rate, escalation rate, cost, and error severity. See Experiment 2.
FalsificationTest: If a simpler baseline (e.g. B4, a fixed rules->retrieval->LLM order with no evidence-driven gating) matches ADS-Cascade's accuracy-cost frontier, the evidence-driven gating adds no demonstrated value over a static pipeline, and the combination claim reduces to 'a reasonable engineering pipeline.'
Risk: No baseline comparison has ever been run. The 98.1%@42.8% figure describes what ADS-Cascade does, not that it does it better than simpler alternatives -- the largest evidentiary gap among all six candidates.

Claim: Romanian fiscal-document (D406/SAF-T) product-to-GL-account classification is a real-world case study establishing the method's applicability, in a domain where commercial vendors 'typically ship a single learned classifier chosen up front rather than derived from a measured determinism distribution.'
PriorArtOverlap: No peer-reviewed academic paper doing SAF-T/D406-specific ML classification was found -- genuine academic under-coverage. But three independent commercial AP-automation vendors (Ken From Finance, Peakflo, Ramp) publicly describe confidence-tiered auto-apply/human-review cascades with correction feedback for invoice GL-coding today; one (Ken From Finance) explicitly recommends a pre-deployment historical-consistency audit, closely mirroring ADS-Cascade's own Part 1.
DistinctiveElement: The academic niche (Romanian D406 specifically) is genuinely under-served. The manuscript's 'no comparable practice exists' framing is directly contradicted by at least one vendor's own public materials.
TechnicalSignificance: None as a methodological claim -- this is inherently a case-study/application contribution, not a technique contribution. Its value is empirical grounding, not novelty.
EmpiricallyTestable: N/A as a novelty claim. The underlying production numbers are the paper's strongest evidence category, but they support 'this works in one real deployment,' not 'this is a new method.'
CurrentEvidence: reports/phase1_final_report.md, EVIDENCE_BASELINE.md production rows: 296,648 invoice lines, 169 companies, 91.2% deterministic, 76,843 mappings, Tier-1 98.4%@42% coverage in live production use.
MissingEvidence: A direct, sourced check of what TECHNICAL_REPORT.md section 5 actually claims about vendor practice, against B8-04/05/06, to confirm or correct the 'vendors don't measure before choosing' framing before publication.
FalsificationTest: N/A for the case-study framing itself. The narrower factual claim ('vendors don't measure history before choosing') is already falsified by B8-04's public materials and must be corrected regardless of Phase C's outcome on the other contributions.
Risk: Low risk if reframed honestly as a case study; high risk (an easily checked factual overclaim) if the current 'no comparable vendor practice' language survives into the manuscript unchanged.
